questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How our bank savings can help or harm the planet
How to save money on energy bills
Why some people still keep money under the mattress
How banks make a profit
questions.why: Beth says they'll discuss ways our money can help protect the environment.

questions.q: What point does Neil make about money in the bank?
options: It is safer than cash at home
It just sits there doing nothing
Banks invest it, sometimes in polluting businesses
It always supports green energy projects around the world
questions.why: He says it's invested to fund other businesses, some far from environmentally friendly.

questions.q: What does Beth mean when she says she is “very green about money”?
options: She only uses eco-friendly banks
She doesn't know much about it
She is jealous of rich people
She spends a lot on green products
questions.why: She says she means green as in ignorant or naïve, not environmentally friendly.

options: A campaign by Richard Curtis
An oil drilling company that opened in Bristol in 2012
A pension fund for teachers
The UK's first environmentally sustainable bank
questions.why: Neil says it was the UK's first environmentally sustainable bank, opened in Bristol in 2012.

questions.q: How has interest in ethical banking changed, according to John Fleetwood?
options: It has almost disappeared
It has always been very popular
It is now mainly for big businesses, not for ordinary people
It used to be for a small group, but has grown hugely
questions.why: He says it was viewed as a niche thing but has now broadened hugely.

questions.q: What is a big concern among investors now?
options: Banks closing down
Some banks pretending to be green without real action
Interest rates going up
There are now far too many ethical funds to choose from
questions.why: Fleetwood says there's great concern about greenwashing – who's jumping on the bandwagon.

questions.q: Why does Beth think banks are likely to change their behaviour?
options: They depend on customers, who can move their money elsewhere
The government has passed new laws that force them to change
Their staff want them to
Oil companies ask them to
questions.why: She says banks rely on customers' money and change when customers threaten to leave.

questions.q: Why did Mark Carney tell Richard Curtis to “go for it”?
options: The accounting and reporting systems were already perfect
Pensions were about to become illegal
More public interest will force companies to be open
Comic Relief needed more money
questions.why: Curtis says Carney told him the more people become interested, the more transparent companies must be.
